solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: They must be held in silence

definitions.text: They must be held in silence

parts.words: They must be held in silence
parts.note: the idiom for keeping quiet tells you to keep your speaking organ still, so these are what a silent person restrains

explanation.surface: A rule about keeping certain secrets during a hush.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'hold your tongue' means stay silent, so these mouth organs are what silent people hold.

clue.text: Kind of noise made by very loud car, it …

indicators.note: something made from these letters is built anew, so the pieces are rearranged

parts.note: FF, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud

explanation.surface: A deafening car, and the din it creates, leading into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made' signals the anagram: FF plus CARIT rearranges to the answer. The ellipsis joins this clue to 2-down, which continues the sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: Traffic noise is the roar of vehicles on roads, a familiar category of urban sound.

clue.text: … is fractionally above the line

parts.note: in a written fraction the top number sits above the dividing line, so 'fractionally' means in a fraction rather than slightly

explanation.surface: Continuing 1-down: the car's noise is just a little over the permitted limit.
explanation.definitionFit: In a vulgar fraction the top figure, written over the bar, is the dividend counted in parts.

clue.text: Extreme leaders of unions never doubt us, ever!

indicators.note: the leaders of the following five words are their opening letters, taken in order

explanation.surface: A rallying cry from trade unions insisting they should never be doubted.
explanation.definitionFit: Undue means excessive, beyond what is warranted, which is an extreme degree.

clue.text: Disabled in boats at sea, take on elderly too

indicators.note: being at sea means confused or all over the place, so the letters of boats are jumbled

parts.note: elderly people are aged

explanation.surface: Disabled passengers in boats on the ocean, with old people taken on board too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disabled' reads as describing people but means wrecked; 'at sea' gives SABOT. 'in', 'take on' and 'too' merely link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sabotaged has been deliberately put out of action, i.e. wrecked so it cannot work.

clue.text: The glass appears to be falling

definitions.meaning: a flat-bottomed drinking vessel without a stem
one who tumbles, an acrobat whose act is falling and rolling

explanation.surface: A barometer reading suggests the pressure is dropping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The glass' and 'falling' evoke a barometer, but the answer is a drinking vessel and, read as an agent noun, one who tumbles.
explanation.definitionFit: A drinking vessel with straight sides is this; an acrobat doing somersaults is also one who takes falls.

clue.text: Flagging — it goes up on sign of danger

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means reading the word it from bottom to top

parts.note: red is the colour that warns of danger

explanation.surface: A flag is hoisted to warn of danger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes up' reverses IT to TI in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Flagging means losing energy, and a weary person is worn out.

clue.text: Charlie's computer accessory that accommodates lively chat

definitions.note: Charlie Chaplin's famous feature was a toothbrush growth on his upper lip

indicators.note: something that accommodates holds others within it, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a mouse is the pointing device for a computer

indicators.note: lively suggests movement, so the letters of chat are stirred around

explanation.surface: A gadget owned by someone named Charlie that hosts animated online conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: Charlie Chaplin's toothbrush growth makes 'Charlie's' a fair definition; 'lively' gives TACH for 'that accommodates' to enclose.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlie Chaplin's trademark was a small clipped growth of hair above the lip, his best-known feature.

clue.text: A small spike that climbs — it's a climber!

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means the letters read upwards, reversed

parts.note: a nail is a small metal spike

explanation.surface: A small spike on a climbing plant, playfully called a climber itself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that climbs' reverses A NAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: A liana is a woody vine of tropical forests that winds up trees, a classic climbing plant.

clue.text: More hasty seconds eaten at breakfast

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for things consumed in the morning, standing for the noun

parts.note: rasher is the comparative of rash, meaning more hasty

explanation.surface: Someone in a hurry grabbing second helpings at breakfast.
explanation.definitionFit: Slices of bacon are a staple of the cooked British morning meal.

clue.text: Capone leaves in a panic, carrying a gun

indicators.note: when Capone leaves, his first name departs from the word

parts.note: alarmed means frightened, in a panic
Al Capone was the Chicago gangster

explanation.surface: A gangster flees in panic while toting a firearm.
explanation.definitionFit: Being armed means bearing weapons, such as a pistol.

clue.text: Islanders have runners going around beating drum

indicators.note: the beans go around the other letters, enclosing them

parts.note: runner beans, so runners can be beans

indicators.note: beating knocks the letters of drum into a new order

explanation.surface: Islanders with athletes circling a drummer pounding a beat.
explanation.walkthrough: Runners here are runner beans, a common British garden vegetable, not athletes; 'beating' gives RMUD for them to go around.
explanation.definitionFit: People from the Atlantic island territory of Bermuda are natives of an island.

clue.text: In exchange of fire Edward gets lost

indicators.note: an exchange swaps things around, so the letters of these words change places

parts.note: Ted is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: Edward is killed or lost in a gunfight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exchange of fire' reads as a gunfight phrase, but 'In exchange' is the anagram signal, giving FORFEI.
explanation.definitionFit: To forfeit something is to lose it as a penalty, so forfeited things are lost.

clue.text: Kid's meals on the phone

definitions.note: read as kid is; to kid is to rib or joke with someone, verb plus 's

indicators.note: words heard on the phone are heard, not seen, so this signals a sound-alike

parts.note: teas are light afternoon or evening meals

explanation.surface: A child's food order is placed by telephone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kid's' reads as 'kid is', so the definition is the verb kid. Tea is a British name for an evening meal.
explanation.definitionFit: To kid someone is to joke with or rib them playfully, which is to mock.

clue.text: A queen, perhaps the Queen, is to provide meals

parts.note: a queen is a female cat, so a cat may be one
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: A royal personage, perhaps the monarch herself, hosting a banquet.
explanation.walkthrough: A queen is a female cat; ER is Elizabeth Regina.
explanation.definitionFit: Caterers supply food for functions; to cater is to provide food.

clue.text: A farthing, maybe, on Victorian transport

definitions.text: A farthing, maybe, on Victorian transport

parts.words: A farthing, maybe, on Victorian transport
parts.note: the penny-farthing bicycle had a huge front wheel (the penny) and a tiny back one (the farthing)

explanation.surface: An old coin found on a nineteenth-century vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: The penny-farthing was a Victorian bicycle; a farthing was the smallest old British coin, hence its small back wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: On a penny-farthing bicycle the small back circle was nicknamed the farthing.

clue.text: Communicate properly — what would-be MP must do

definitions.meaning: a candidate needs voters to put an X, a cross, by their name on ballot papers

explanation.surface: Advice to a parliamentary candidate to put the message across.
explanation.walkthrough: Voters in UK elections mark their choice with a cross; MP is Member of Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: To make your point understood is to put it over clearly; a candidate also needs to obtain voters' marks.

clue.text: Old ways of revolution with ancient weapons

parts.note: a turn is one revolution
pikes were long spears of old armies

explanation.surface: Historic routes taken during an uprising armed with ancient arms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolution' suggests uprising but means a rotation.
explanation.definitionFit: Turnpikes were historic toll roads, so they are old routes.

clue.text: Mostly crooked gas- and oil- rich Russians?

definitions.text: Mostly crooked gas- and oil- rich Russians?

indicators.note: crooked means bent out of shape, so the letters are twisted into a new order
mostly means not quite all, so one letter of the last word is dropped

explanation.surface: A jibe at Russian tycoons enriched by fuel, mostly dishonest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' drops an I from RICH to leave RCH; 'crooked' rearranges GAS, OIL and RCH. The whole clue also describes the tycoons.
explanation.definitionFit: Russian tycoons who made fortunes from post-Soviet energy privatisation are known as a ruling few.

clue.text: Herb's record-playing welcomes Scot aboard

definitions.note: read as herb is, the 's a link to the rest

indicators.note: to welcome is to take in, so one piece goes inside another
aboard means taken on, inside the other piece
playing about with the letters of record rearranges them

parts.note: Ian is a typically Scottish first name

explanation.surface: A man called Herb spins records and invites a Scotsman onto his boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Herb' looks like a man's name but is the plant; 'playing' gives CORDER, and 'welcomes ... aboard' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Coriander is a leafy plant used in cooking, also called cilantro.

clue.text: Finding fault with fish, take a gin cocktail

parts.note: a carp is a freshwater fish

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters of gin are mixed

explanation.surface: Complaining about the fish course and reaching for a gin drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cocktail' rearranges GIN into ING.
explanation.definitionFit: Carping is persistent nagging complaint, criticising over trifles.

clue.text: Musical key almost essential

parts.note: E is a musical key

indicators.note: almost means not quite the whole word, so its last letter goes

parts.note: vital means essential

explanation.surface: A key signature that is nearly indispensable to a song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims VITAL to VITA.
explanation.definitionFit: Evita is the Lloyd Webber and Rice stage show about Eva Perón.

clue.text: Classic advice to cheat the years

definitions.meaning: timeless, never going out of style
read as two words, ..., an instruction to grow old more slowly

explanation.surface: Time-honoured tips on staying young.
explanation.definitionFit: Something timeless never dates, which is what a classic is; split, it urges one to grow old less.

clue.text: Descartes gets wife to modernise

parts.note: René Descartes, the French philosopher

explanation.surface: A philosopher marries in order to update his thinking.
explanation.definitionFit: To renew is to restore or make fresh, which is to update.

clue.text: South African place of birth

definitions.meaning: the former province on South Africa's east coast
relating to being born, as in prenatal

explanation.surface: Someone's South African birthplace.
explanation.definitionFit: Natal was a province of South Africa; the adjective also means relating to being born.

clue.text: Pagan hero provides a home for little Annie

indicators.note: the letters provide the material for something new, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A heathen champion offers shelter to a small girl.
explanation.walkthrough: Little Orphan Annie is the comic-strip girl of the musical Annie, raised in a children's home.
explanation.definitionFit: Annie of the strip and musical grew up in an institution for parentless children.

clue.text: Female duck not recorded

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nought, O
a live performance is broadcast as it happens, not recorded

explanation.surface: A female duck that escaped being documented.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Female' defines a woman's name; a duck is a zero score in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Olive is a woman's given name, so it can stand for a female.

clue.text: Spotted potential in dance

indicators.note: potential means what could be, so the letters could become another word

explanation.surface: Someone saw promise in a dancer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spotted' suggests noticed but means pimply.
explanation.definitionFit: Acned skin is marked by pimples, so it is blemished with spots.

clue.text: Healthy location right here!

definitions.meaning: an idiom for in excellent health
the FT is printed on pink paper, so this clue sits literally on the pink

explanation.surface: A cheerful claim that this very spot is good for you.
explanation.walkthrough: The Financial Times is printed on salmon-pink paper, so the clue itself is located on pink.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in fine health; the puzzle also sits on the newspaper's coloured paper.

clue.text: Specialist area in hospital that's pleasant outside

indicators.note: the word for pleasant is outside, wrapping the abbreviation

parts.note: nice means pleasant

explanation.surface: A medical specialism inside a hospital with nice grounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A niche is a specialised segment, as in a niche market.

clue.text: Possibly illegal eastern junk one left in the sea

indicators.note: junk as a verb means scrap, so these letters are thrown together anew

parts.note: the clue word itself, taken as written
one L, the abbreviation for left, is the letter to come out of the mix

explanation.surface: Smuggled goods, possibly, dumped from a Chinese boat into the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'junk' anagrams ILLEGAL plus E after one L is set aside. 'junk' tempts as a Chinese boat. 'Possibly' marks the definition: the Sea of Galilee.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sea of Galilee is the freshwater lake in northern Israel.

clue.text: Island sin sites regularly chosen by deviants

indicators.note: letters chosen at regular intervals, every second one

explanation.surface: Perverts choosing islands for wicked resorts.
explanation.definitionFit: People who take pleasure in cruelty are a type of deviant.
